title: Domande e Parole Interrogative
subtitle: Ask yes/no questions and use the question words: chi, cosa, dove, quando, perché, come, quanto.
objectives: Form a yes/no question with no word-order change
Use the seven core question words

content.intro: Forming a question in Italian is refreshingly simple: for yes/no questions, the word order usually doesn't change at all.
content.explanation: A statement becomes a yes/no question just by using rising intonation in speech, or a question mark in writing — Parli italiano. becomes Parli italiano? with no other change. For questions asking for information, place the question word at the start of the sentence.

rules.heading: a) Yes/no questions
rules.body: Same word order as the statement, just rising intonation / a question mark: Sei italiano? Hai fame? Vuoi un caffè?

rules.heading: b) The seven question words
rules.body:
• chi — who: Chi è?
  • cosa / che cosa — what: Cosa fai?
  • dove — where: Dove abiti?
  • quando — when: Quando parti?
  • perché — why: Perché studi l'italiano?
  • come — how: Come stai?
  • quanto/a/i/e — how much/many (agrees like an adjective): Quanti anni hai?

rules.heading: c) Answering perché
rules.body: Perché means both "why" and "because" — context (and a comma, in writing) tells them apart: Perché studi l'italiano? Perché mi piace. (Why do you study Italian? Because I like it.)

examples.it: Perché sei triste? Perché ho perso il lavoro.
examples.en: Why are you sad? Because I lost my job.
How many siblings do you have?
How do you say "thank you" in English?

commonMistakes.why: Question words go at the start of the sentence, not at the end as in some casual English word order.
Quanto agrees like an adjective — sorelle is feminine plural, so it must be quante.

commonMistakes.wrong: Do you speak Spanish? — Fai tu parlare spagnolo?
commonMistakes.why: Italian doesn't use a "do/does" auxiliary for questions — just use the plain conjugated verb.

items.explanation: "Come ti chiami" — how are you called — is the standard way to ask a name.
Anni is masculine plural, so quanto agrees as quanti.
Chi asks "who", the right word for asking about a person.

summary: Yes/no questions in Italian use the same word order as the statement — only intonation/punctuation changes.
The seven core question words: chi, cosa, dove, quando, perché, come, quanto (which agrees like an adjective).
Perché means both "why" and "because" — the same word covers both sides of the exchange.
